How Bees Make Honey

By Maya Fernandes · March 14, 2024

Honey is one of the oldest sweeteners people know, yet very few of us have watched how it is made. Inside every hive, thousands of worker bees share the job, passing nectar from bee to bee until it slowly turns into the thick golden food we spread on toast.

This guide walks through each stage, from the moment a forager lands on a flower to the moment a beekeeper lifts a full frame out of the box. You can read more on the beekeeping basics page if you are new to the topic.

Step one: collecting nectar¶

Forager bees visit hundreds of flowers on a single trip. They drink the sugary nectar with a long tongue and store it in a special honey stomach that is separate from the stomach they use for their own food. Our hive tools guide explains the kit.

Step two: turning nectar into honey

Back at the hive, the nectar is handed to house bees. Enzymes added by the bees break the sugars down, and the bees fan their wings over the open cells so that extra water evaporates.

  • Nectar starts out as roughly eighty percent water.
  • Finished honey holds less than twenty percent water.
  • The bees seal each full cell with a wax cap.

What a single hive produces

SeasonHoney per hive
Spring5 kg
Summer15 kg

Beekeepers only take the extra honey, leaving enough behind so the colony can survive the winter months when no flowers are in bloom.
